title: The Confidence Heuristic and How to Use Confidence
summary: The creator explains the concept of the confidence heuristic, where people assume a confident person knows more, and breaks down when and how to appropriately use confidence or admit ignorance based on the situation.
key_points: Confidence heuristic: People naturally treat a speaker's poise, steady voice, and firm tone as a reliable proxy for expertise and good information.
Confidence works like a loan; it can be borrowed for the time being, but a loan has to be repaid.
Green Zone: When you know something thoroughly through first-person experience, say it plainly and avoid phrases like 'I think'.
Yellow Zone: When you half-know it, focus on direction rather than exact details/specifics (example: 'My read is this, but I'll confirm by tomorrow').
Red Zone: When stakes are high and you do not know the facts, admit you do not know yet, provide a specific time when you will get back with an action plan, and stop talking.
Jessica Pearson's strategy: Silence can be the strongest move in the room when used wisely.
content: hope you learnt something new today pt.41 #thementalist #growth #confidence #harveyspecter #success [ forensic science, confidence, science, patrick jane, donna paulsen, harvey specter, jessica pearson, scientific research, confidence heuristic, educational, hopecore, personal growth, skills, speaking skills, success, mindset ] Harvey Specter, Patrick Jane, Donna Paulsen, Jessica Pearson, TV's most confident characters, and yet we copy them entirely wrong. Hi, I'm Gaurika, forensic science student and in under 3 minutes, I'm going to give you a map to keep confidence on your side. Stay till the end because this is the one thing that we have all mistaken about. Let's start with Patrick Jane. In one scene he says, it's smart to seem like you know your stuff because it fosters trust. That is confidence heuristic. According to psychologists, people assume that a confident person knows more. So confidence works like a loan. You can borrow it for the time being. But a loan has to be repaid and Jane knows it. In another scene he tells Lisbon that what are the chances of him being wrong second or two times in a row? Now that's not just bravado, it's his personal track record that he has kept over all these years. And research agrees, we also track whether your confidence has been right before. Someone who is sure when they know and honest when they don't, will earn more credibility than someone who is just always very sure. So here's the map that I promised you. It is evaluated into three zones: green zone, yellow zone, and red zone. Green zone: It is when you know something, you've practiced it, you've done it, basically experienced something. This is also something that you can show proof for. Say it plainly. It is this, you don't have to say I think, no. That is what Donna Paulsen does, she knows what she's going to talk about. It is only after a very thorough research that you fall into the green zone. Then the yellow zone: You half know it. In this case you have to be sure of the direction but you're not going to describe everything to the tee. You can say something like, my read is this, but I'll confirm by tomorrow. Now that deadline is what is a loan and you will have to repay it at. Jane and Harvey do it all the time. They have a plan, but they're not very sure of the details, that is exactly what they go on a hunt for later. And then the red zone: This is urgent. You don't know, or either the stakes are high like health, money, reputation, or even safety for that matter. These are the times when someone can check then and there about your claims being right or wrong. Simply say, I don't know yet, but I will get back to you with a specific time. If possible, even give them an action plan that you are going to follow. Then, stop talking. That is what Jessica Pearson does, she knows that sometimes silence can be the strongest move in the room and she uses it very wisely. I've personally seen a lot of people walk into rooms, unsure of something, they go back, do their homework, come back stronger with a report. Now this is the report that everyone is actually concerned about. They don't know what's going on here, they don't want to understand that. Your mental process, your intention, your hard work, everything that you personally did is none of anyone else's concern. It is, however, very concerning for you. So you have to do your homework and get back in a stipulated time. That is what builds a rapport. Now tell me, have you ever sounded sure of something you didn't know yet? And did you pay it back? Let me know in the comments and save this for your next big meeting. Follow because this is the science of being human.
